interfaces.why: Each Lambda function has an Events.*.Type: Api declaration (HTTP GET/POST/DELETE at /orders and /orders/{order_id}) that constitutes declared HTTP handler interfaces, but the SAM Api event type does not match any of the supported interface kinds in the dircue vocabulary (no CLI binary, declared port, gRPC service, Spring Boot application, or npm start). capabilities.why: DynamoDB client (software.amazon.awssdk:dynamodb) confirmed from pom.xml:77; apache-client HTTP transport labeled with ambiguity note; transitive AWS SDK dependencies may introduce other clients not visible in pom.xml first-party dependencies

The SAM Globals section (template.yaml:9-16) sets TABLE_NAME and ENDPOINT_OVERRIDE environment variables for all functions; ENDPOINT_OVERRIDE is empty string in production but used for DynamoDB Local in integration tests (pom.xml:362 docker-maven-plugin).

template.yaml:2 Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31 marks this as a SAM template, not a raw CloudFormation template; SAM expands functions with Api events into an implicit AWS::Serverless::Api resource (API Gateway), but this implicit resource is not an explicit declaration.

Runtime java8 is specified; this is Lambda runtime java8 (Amazon Linux 2 with Java 8 Corretto), not literally JDK 1.8.

components.why: Oracle files cover root module plus 3 sub-directories; wrappers/vpc-endpoints/, wrappers/flow-log/, and all examples/* directories contain .tf files but are not in oracle files

deployables.why: Same scope as components; at least 6 additional .tf directories (wrappers/vpc-endpoints, wrappers/flow-log, examples/complete, examples/simple, examples/outpost, examples/ipv6) are not covered

interfaces.why: Terraform modules declare no CLI binaries, EXPOSE ports, gRPC services, or Spring Boot applications; no supported interface kind applies to infrastructure-as-code module declarations

capabilities.why: This is a networking infrastructure module; it provisions AWS VPC resources but declares no application-level service dependencies (datastores, caches, queues, HTTP clients) that map to the capability catalog

edges.why: The wrapper-to-root dependency edge is captured; modules/vpc-endpoints and modules/flow-log are not called by any oracle file, so their call-site edges are unknown

notes: The root module and modules/vpc-endpoints/versions.tf have identical SHA-256 hashes, meaning their versions.tf files are byte-for-byte identical.
modules/flow-log/versions.tf has a higher required_version (>= 1.5.7) than the root module (>= 1.0); this is notable for compatibility labeling.
wrappers/vpc-endpoints/ and wrappers/flow-log/ are additional wrapper modules not in oracle files; they follow the same pattern as wrappers/main.tf.

Terraform modules do not expose application-layer interfaces (no ports, no CLI) in the dircue vocabulary; interface and capability coverage is structurally unknown for any pure Terraform module repository.

The root module's main.tf creates AWS VPC, public/private/database/elasticache/redshift/intra subnets, internet gateway, NAT gateway, and route tables; these are AWS infrastructure resources, not dircue deployable sub-items.
The provider_meta 'aws' user_agent identifies the module as github.com/terraform-aws-modules/terraform-aws-vpc in both root and sub-modules.

label_corrections.reason: settings.gradle:1 declares rootProject.name = 'spring-petclinic'; this is the canonical gradle project name. Added to oracle_files so the gradle component name can be verified correctly.
superset-websocket/Dockerfile is not in oracle_files; the label claimed a container_build from a non-oracle file. Removed. The service 'superset-websocket' in docker-compose.yml is still labeled.

label_corrections.correction: Removed all 4 terraform components. dircue puts Terraform modules into kind=deployable/infrastructure, not kind=component. MAP.md explicitly lists Terraform under deployables. Having them in components is a label error caused by the category-(c) schema difference.

Added modules/vpc-endpoints/main.tf and modules/flow-log/main.tf to oracle_files. dircue derives deployable evidence from resource blocks in main.tf, not versions.tf. The labeler chose versions.tf as oracle files assuming they would be the evidence source, but dircue uses main.tf.

Changed name 'wrapper' to 'wrappers'. dircue names terraform deployables from the directory path (wrappers/), not the Terraform module block name (module "wrapper"). This is a convention difference - label used the block name, dircue uses the directory name.
